{{Short description|Swiss crystallographer}}

'''Hans-Beat Bürgi''' (born 20 January 1942, [[Münsterlingen]]) is a Swiss chemist and [[Crystallography|crystallographer]]. He was a professor for crystallography at the [[University of Bern]] from 1979 to 2007.

== Education and career ==
Bürgi attended primary and secondary school in Kreuzlingen. He went on to study chemistry at the [[ETH Zurich]] from which he graduated in 1965. He gained his doctoral degree at the ETH Zurich in 1969 under the supervision of [[Jack D. Dunitz]]. For his post-doctoral studies, he joined [[Lawrence Bartell]] at the University of Michigan. Upon his return to the ETH Zurich, he was an oberassistent and independent group leader from 1971 to 1979. In 1975, he completed his habilitation in general and structural chemistry.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Prof Dr. Hans-Beat Bürgi|url=http://www.chem.uzh.ch/en/research/groups/linden/buergi/curriculumVitae.html|access-date=2022-01-20|website=www.chem.uzh.ch|language=en}}</ref>

At the University of Bern, Bürgi was professor for [[X-ray crystallography]] from 1979 until his official retirement in 2007. During this time and beyond, he was visiting professor at [[Princeton University]], [[Australian National University]], [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology|Technion]], [[California Institute of Technology|CALTECH]], [[Tokyo Institute of Technology]], [[University of California, Berkeley|University of California]] and [[University of Western Australia|the University of Western Australia]]. Since 2007, he is a permanent academic guest at the [[University of Zurich]] and organiser of the annual Zurich School of Crystallography.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Zurich School of Cystallography|url=https://www.chem.uzh.ch/linden/zsc/|access-date=2022-01-20|website=www.chem.uzh.ch}}</ref>

== Research ==
At the ETH Zurich, Bürgi investigated chemical reaction paths with Jack Dunitz which led to the description concept of structure correlation. In organic chemistry, the [[Bürgi–Dunitz angle|Bürgi-Dunitz angle]] of nucleophilic attack at [[carbonyl group]]s is a widely used descriptor.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Burgi|first1=H. B.|last2=Dunitz|first2=J. D.|last3=Shefter|first3=Eli.|date=July 1973|title=Geometrical reaction coordinates. II. Nucleophilic addition to a carbonyl group|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ja00796a058|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|language=en|volume=95|issue=15|pages=5065–5067|doi=10.1021/ja00796a058|issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref> It originated from collaborative work with [[Jean-Marie Lehn]]'s group in Strasbourg.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bürgi|first1=H.B.|last2=Dunitz|first2=J.D.|last3=Lehn|first3=J.M.|last4=Wipff|first4=G.|date=January 1974|title=Stereochemistry of reaction paths at carbonyl centres|url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0040402001906787|journal=Tetrahedron|language=en|volume=30|issue=12|pages=1563–1572|doi=10.1016/S0040-4020(01)90678-7|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Beyond accurate chemical crystallography and [[quantum crystallography]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Grabowsky|first1=Simon|last2=Genoni|first2=Alessandro|last3=Bürgi|first3=Hans-Beat|date=2017|title=Quantum crystallography|url=http://xlink.rsc.org/?DOI=C6SC05504D|journal=Chemical Science|language=en|volume=8|issue=6|pages=4159–4176|doi=10.1039/C6SC05504D|issn=2041-6520|pmc=5576428|pmid=28878872}}</ref> Bürgi's research focuses on dynamics in crystals as well as disorder and diffuse scattering.<ref>{{Cite web|title=International School of Crystallography :: Welcome|url=https://crystalerice.org/2022/|access-date=2022-01-20|website=crystalerice.org}}</ref> His interpretation of atomic and lattice vibrations in crystals always provides a link to chemistry. Bürgi and coworkers have created tools such as normal coordinate analysis to derive thermodynamic properties from [[X-ray crystallography|X-ray diffraction]] data<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bürgi|first1=H. B.|last2=Capelli|first2=S. C.|date=2000-09-01|title=Dynamics of molecules in crystals from multi-temperature anisotropic displacement parameters. I. Theory|url=http://scripts.iucr.org/cgi-bin/paper?S0108767300005626|journal=Acta Crystallographica Section A|volume=56|issue=5|pages=403–412|doi=10.1107/S0108767300005626|pmid=10967519|issn=0108-7673|url-access=subscription}}</ref> or PEANUT to display atomic displacement parameters and differences thereof.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hummel|first1=W.|last2=Raselli|first2=A.|last3=Bürgi|first3=H.-B.|date=1990-10-01|title=Analysis of atomic displacement parameters and molecular motion in crystals|url=http://scripts.iucr.org/cgi-bin/paper?S0108768190006334|journal=Acta Crystallographica Section B |volume=46|issue=5|pages=683–692|doi=10.1107/S0108768190006334|s2cid=94630827 |issn=0108-7681|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

He has published over 200 peer-reviewed articles and edited two books.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Publications|url=http://www.chem.uzh.ch/en/research/groups/linden/buergi/publications.html|access-date=2022-01-20|website=www.chem.uzh.ch|language=en}}</ref>

== Awards ==
Bürgi was awarded the Werner prize for young Swiss scientists by the [[Swiss Chemical Society]] in 1975.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Awards: Werner Prize|url=https://scg.ch/component/page/werner|access-date=2022-01-20|website=Swiss Chemical Society|language=en-gb|archive-date=2022-01-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220120103359/https://scg.ch/component/page/werner|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2022, the journal [[Acta Crystallographica|Acta Crystallographica B]] published a special issue on "Structure Correlation and Dynamics in Crystals", honouring Bürgi on the occasion of his 80th birthday.<ref>{{Cite web|title=(IUCr) Acta Crystallographica Section B - special issues|url=https://journals.iucr.org/b/services/specialissues.html|access-date=2022-01-20|website=journals.iucr.org}}</ref>
